prerequisites: Knowledge of general materials technologies, in particular: the graphic representation of mechanical parts and the understanding of the prescriptions given; the definitions and the metallurgical and mechanical properties of main engineering materials; the effects of heat treatments

learning_outcomes.text: Student knows: subtractive manufacturing processes (cutting mechanism, turning, milling, drilling, rectilinear cutting processes, grinding); conservative processing processes (forging and molding, rolling, drawing, extrusion, metal sheet forming); foundry processes; autogene and heterogeneous welding processes.

The student is able to: choose the most appropriate manufacturing process to create surfaces meeting the specific design requirements; calculate force and power required for processing; select tools and equipment to perform a specific process; evaluate the feasibility of processing with specified equipment and machines.
Being able to identify the most appropriate processes to create surfaces meeting the specific design requirements.
Being able to describe, in written form, in a clear and concise way and orally present the objectives using technical-scientific language, the procedure and the results of the performed elaborations.
Being able to apply the knowledge acquired in contexts different from those presented during the course, and to deepen the topics covered using materials other than those proposed.

syllabus_topics: CASTING PROCESSES, FOUNDRY MODELS, FOUNDRY SANDS, PREPARATION OF THE SAND, MECHANICAL FORMING, METAL CASTING, MELTING FURNACES.
MACHINING PROCESSES (THEORY HOURS 26, EXERCITATIVE HOURS 10, LABORATORY HOURS 4)
SHORT NOTES ON GEOMETRICAL AND DIMENSIONAL TOLERANCES.
MATERIALS AND GEOMETRY OF CUTTING TOOLS.
MACHINE TOOLS: STRUCTURE, COMPONENTS, AND WORKING PRINCIPLE.
PLANNING AND VERIFICATION OF MACHINING OPERATION.
assessment_rules: The final grade is expressed in thirtieths. To access the oral exam, the written test must be passed with a minimum score of 18/30. The final mark is obtained as the average of the written and oral tests. The minimum assessment grade (18/30) is attributed for a limited understanding of manufacturing processes and poor display capacity. The maximum grade (30/30) is attributed for complete knowledge, problem-solving ability, and remarkable planning and presentation skills. Honors may be awarded for significant mastery, language properties, and autonomous processing capacity.
